name: Could Not Dispatch
description: Plays a looping image or video when every real stream on a channel has failed, so viewers see a message instead of a black screen. With an API key, it later sends the channel back to its first stream.
author: PilaScat

fields.label: Image or video
fields.help_text: A path inside the Dispatcharr data volume, or an http(s) link that is downloaded and cached. The message must already be part of the file.

fields.label: Image or video when the provider is full
fields.help_text: Optional, given like the one above. Shown instead of it to a channel whose every source belongs to a provider account that was at its connection limit in the last 20 seconds, so the message can say that every connection is in use. Needs the API key. Empty: the same card for every channel.

fields.label: Show the channels in use
fields.help_text: Writes on the card for a full provider the channels that hold its connections, one per line, with the programme on now when the guide has one. Leave the picture empty where the lines go, set just below.

fields.label: Height of the channels in use (%)
fields.help_text: Where the first line starts, as a share of the picture's height from the top, between 0 and 95. 58.5 puts it at 632 px on a 1080p card.

fields.label: Font for the channels in use
fields.help_text: Optional: a .ttf, .otf or .ttc file inside the Dispatcharr data volume. Empty: the sans-serif font of the container.

fields.label: Local port
fields.help_text: Port the fallback stream listens on, inside the Dispatcharr container. Change it only on a conflict.

fields.label: Width (px)
fields.help_text: 0 matches the picture, up to 1920x1080. Width and height are a pair: set both, or leave both at 0.

fields.label: Frames per second
fields.help_text: Keep it at the rate of your channels: Jellyfin keeps the frame rate a session starts with, so a viewer who starts on the card at 5 stays at 5 after the channel is back.

fields.label: Stream bitrate (kbit/s)
fields.help_text: The fallback is padded to this constant rate. Lowering it costs picture quality on dark gradients and makes the card appear later, since Dispatcharr buffers 1 MB before showing anything.

fields.label: Excluded groups
fields.help_text: One channel group name per line. Those channels keep failing as before.

fields.label: Excluded channels
fields.help_text: One channel number or channel name per line.

fields.label: Cover new channels automatically
fields.help_text: Attaches the fallback to channels added by an M3U refresh.

fields.label: API key
fields.help_text: A Dispatcharr API key. With it, a channel left on the fallback goes back to its first stream after two minutes, then at longer intervals, or as soon as a connection frees up when it fell back for lack of one. Empty keeps channels on the fallback.

actions.label: Apply settings
actions.description: Applies the settings above and covers every channel that is not excluded.

actions.label: Check status
actions.description: Reports whether the fallback is running and how many channels carry it.

actions.label: Cover new channels
actions.description: Covers channels that do not carry the fallback yet.

actions.label: Restart fallback
actions.description: Starts the fallback again if it is down.

actions.label: Remove fallback
actions.description: Detaches it everywhere, stops it and deletes its streams.

confirm.title: Remove the fallback?
confirm.message: Channels go back to failing with an error when every stream is down.
